paras: The Cincinnati near-riot of 1919 was a street fight in Cincinnati, Ohio, that began when white men struck a Black child and Black men returned to the scene. Police arrived in force and ended the fight, and the Cleveland Advocate reported the episode in June 1919 as a race riot "narrowly averted."

According to the Advocate's brief, the trouble "started over the striking of a Colored child by white men." The child's mother told "men of her race" about the assault, and they went back to the scene, where "a general fight" followed. Police then arrived "in force sufficient to quell the affair."
The brief gives no date for the fight, no location within the city, and no names for the child, the mother or the men involved.
The coverage does not report injuries, arrests or any later court action.

The only report found ran on the front page of the Cleveland Advocate on 21 June 1919, in a column of short race-news items under a Cincinnati dateline. Its headline, printed as "RACE BIOT AVERTED," presented the episode as a riot that did not happen, even though the text described a general fight. The brief placed the cause with the white men who struck the child, credited the police with stopping the fight, and offered no editorial comment.
The same column carried unrelated items, including a drowning in Augusta, Georgia, and a graduation at the Ohio Institute for Deaf, Dumb and Blind.

accounts.label: Black-press brief (Cincinnati dateline)
accounts.gist: A race riot was narrowly averted after white men struck a Colored child; Black men returned to the scene, a general fight followed, and police in force ended it.

framing.detail: The Cleveland Advocate ran a short unsigned brief headed 'RACE BIOT AVERTED' that names the white men's striking of a Colored child as the cause and credits the police with quelling the fight.

quotes: A race riot was narrowly averted here, which started over the striking of a Colored child by white men.
The mother of the child reported to men of her race the assault, and they returned to the scene, a general fight resulting.
Police arrived in time in force sufficient to quell the affair.

set_aside: Column of race-news briefs; its Cincinnati item is about Dr. F. A. Williams returning from a business trip, not a riot.
